start.text: You saw. The bridge underneath our rail was exploited. Not my contract: the bridge. It doesn't matter to anyone whose money is stuck.
The operators are tracing the funds. I never asked anyone to trust me blindly. I asked them to trust code. Code has authors, and authors make mistakes.
So the whole idea was a mistake?
No. Wires fail too, just more slowly and with more paperwork. We replaced one kind of trust with another: fewer middlemen, more software.
We solved one trust problem and created another. Same question as always: who holds your money in between?
